newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up, fronts hit new highs again.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up, fronts hit new highs again.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, reversing an early profit-taking pullback, ended up Friday in moderate trade, with front months driven to new highs by technical buying when downside momentum stalled, sources said.

September, which dipped early to $2.375 per million British thermal units, rallied late to a new contract high of $2.53 before closing at $2.503, up 5.9 cents. October, which also hit a new benchmark of $2.53 today, settled 6.3 cents higher at $2.515. Other deferreds ended up by one to 6.3 cents.

"We hit support early and held, then everyone decided to take it higher, but I still think this is a house of cards ready to fall," said one Midwest trader, noting weaker cash prices today and little weather support on the horizon.
Traders said growing concerns about storage after three surprisingly-low weekly stock builds helped turn sentiment more bullish and drive September up 18 percent since late July.
Though overall inventories are still 7.5 percent above last year's record lows, they still lag the 1994-1995 average by more than 400 bcf.
But some noted weekly injections of just 68 bcf are needed through Oct to get stocks back to 2.8 tcf.

Warmer temperatures are forecast for the Northeast into early next week, with heat expected to continue in the Southwest. The Midwest and Southeast should range from normal to below-normal for the period.

Chart traders pegged September resistance at the new contract high of $2.53, with further selling likely in the spot continuation gap between $2.64 and $2.89 from late January. Support was seen in the $2.34 area and then at $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27. Further support points were at $2.20, $2.15-2.16 and then along the short-term up trendline near $2.15.

In the cash Friday, weekend Gulf Coast prices skidded almost 15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.30s. Midcon pipes slipped a similar amount to the mid-$2.20s. New York city gate gas tumbled a dime to the low-$2.50s.

The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose four cents to $2.392. NYMEX Hub open interest for August 7 jumped 8,813 contracts to 208,838. NYMEX volume figures again were unavailable today due to technical problems at the exchange.

On the KCBT, September finished 6.5 cents higher at $2.405, while deferreds ended up by one to 7.1 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 9.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 689 lots traded, up from Thursday's total of 239.
